mechanism: BTC is Phemex/crypto-wide the deepest-liquidity, fastest-price-discovery instrument; thinner-book altcoins have slower market-maker requoting and less informed order flow, so a sizeable BTC impulse is not fully priced into a thin alt's book within the same bar. Published high-frequency Granger-causality work finds a unidirectional BTC->altcoin information-transmission lag, larger for lower-liquidity names. The thesis bets that a >=200bps 3-bar (3h) BTC move that has not yet been matched by an alt implies the alt is still catching up, and rides that catch-up same-direction over the next few closed 1h bars.
counterparty: Passive/slow market-makers and retail limit-order posters on thin altcoin books (DOGE/XRP/SOL/ADA/LINK) who have not yet repriced their quotes after a BTC-driven flow shock; the bot's directional entry captures part of the catch-up move before their books converge to the new BTC-implied level.
prediction: On 1h mr_edge train data (era=train), entering long/short an alt in the same direction as a >=200bps trailing-3-bar BTC move, held up to 8 bars with a 200bps symmetric TP/SL, produces a net_bps_mean whose bootstrap CI95 (bootstrap_ci.mean_ci) excludes 0, with observed WR >= p_star(200)=0.52875 (fee_math.p_star), pooled across the 5-symbol universe.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 2 (short-horizon reversion, alt-vs-ETH, high-vol) is a MEAN-REVERSION bet that died as regime-luck with no sourced mechanism. This thesis is a MOMENTUM-CONTINUATION bet off an external leading instrument (BTC, not ETH), sourced to a published unidirectional Granger-causality/liquidity-lag finding, not a walk-forward-fragile reversion pattern.

Row 5 (cross-sectional momentum) died because it needs a ~100-470-name long/short basket to work and its short leg was dead. This thesis is not cross-sectional at all: each alt is scored independently against an EXTERNAL leading asset (BTC), not ranked against the other names in the universe, and it is long/short per-symbol directional rather than a basket spread.

Row 6 (liquidation-cascade reversion) died specifically because 'high-vol bars CONTINUE, don't revert' -- that finding is consistent with, not contradictory to, this thesis's continuation direction; it is cited because it is the nearest existing verdict on the direction of post-impulse behavior on this account's own data, not because the mechanism is the same (row 6 was a reversion bet on the SAME symbol's own vol spike; this thesis is an inter-asset transmission bet from BTC onto a different, thinner-book symbol).

Row 13 (BTC-TSM(28,5)) is BTC's own daily self-trend/time-series-momentum signal traded on BTC itself and failed the deflated-Sharpe bar. This thesis never trades BTC -- it uses BTC's realized move purely as an external leading signal to trade OTHER (altcoin) instruments at a much shorter horizon (1h/3-bar lookback vs 28-day).

evidence: Kurihara & Matsumoto, 'Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy', Asia-Pacific Financial Markets (2026), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10690-026-09589-z -- per search-result summaries of the published abstract/findings (full text paywalled, not read beyond abstract-level summary): Granger causality tests find a unidirectional BTC->altcoin relationship (their high-frequency data shows an effect as fast as one minute), small-cap / lower-liquidity altcoins show significantly delayed responses to BTC moves, and a BTC-lag trading strategy outperformed buy-and-hold for every tested coin except LTC and ETH. Separately, S&P Global's Bitcoin Volatility Trends report (https://www.spglobal.com/en/research-insights/special-reports/bitcoin-volatility-trends-deep-dive) reports a daily-return correlation near -0.16 between DXY and BTC with NO Granger causality running from DXY to BTC -- used here to rule the equities/DXY leg of this lens OUT (no sourced causal mechanism found) and to justify concentrating this thesis on the BTC-to-altcoin transmission leg instead, where a real causal/liquidity mechanism is published.

spec.doa_line: Kill on first read of screens/cross_asset_btc_lead_alt_lag/out.json if net_bps_mean's bootstrap_ci.mean_ci includes 0, or if observed wr < fee_math.p_star(200)=0.52875, or if n < 30 -- no re-tuning of THRESH_BPS/LOOKBACK/tp_bps/sl_bps after that read.

signal_py:
"""cross_asset_btc_lead_alt_lag: long/short an altcoin in the same direction as a
recent >=200bps trailing-3-bar BTC move, betting on delayed price transmission from
BTC (deep liquidity, fast price discovery) into thinner-book altcoins. Causal: only
uses BTC bars at or before the current (already-closed) bar of the symbol being
scored; reindex/ffill onto the scored symbol's own index means truncating that
symbol's df to a prefix necessarily truncates the BTC lookup to the same prefix.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import pandas as pd
from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld

LOOKBACK = 3        # trailing BTC bars (3h on the 1h timeframe this spec registers)
THRESH_BPS = 200.0  # BTC move required to fire, in bps


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv("BTC", "1h", era="train", dataset="mr_edge")
    if len(df.index) > 0:
        btc = btc[btc.index <= df.index.max()]
    btc_ret_bps = (btc["close"] / btc["close"].shift(LOOKBACK) - 1) * 1e4
    b = btc_ret_bps.reindex(df.index).ffill()
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[b > THRESH_BPS] = 1
    sig[b < -THRESH_BPS] = -1
    return sig
